newsitem.title: USA: US senators -- safeguard deferred payment contracts.
newsitem.headline: US senators -- safeguard deferred payment contracts.

text.p: Four U.S. senators said Thursday they would submit a bill next year to prevent Internal Revenue Service from changing tax rules on deferred payment contracts, a popular way for farmers to market grain.
In a statement, the senators decried the approach taken by the IRS for calculating the alternative minimum tax for an Idaho potato farmer who used one type of a deferred pay plan.

Senators Byron Dorgan, North Dakota Democrat, and Charles Grassley, Iowa Republican, said the IRS approach was "unfar, is not supported by law and imposes an unintended and unacceptable financial hardship on farmers."

The IRS approach was described in a tecnical advice memo released earlier this year. It has inspired concern in farm country although analysts say few farmers face AMT payments or use the type of deferred contract that was at issue.
An IRS spokeswoman has said technical advice memos apply only to one taxpayer and the issues at stake in a dispute.
Dorgan and Grassley said they would file legislation to override the IRS approach and assure traditional tax treatment of deferred payment contracts.
Senators Slade Gorton, Washington state Republican, and Max Baucus, Montana Democrat, would be cosponsors.
American Farm Bureau Federation has written to senators to urge legislation that would block the IRS from seeking back taxes from farmers who use deferred payment contracts.
AFBF says tax law should be changed to ensure that income from such contracts was not counted in AMT calculatons.
Dean Kleckner, AFBF president, said farmers deserved the exemption because deferred payment contracts were a way to even out fluctuations in yields and market prices.
In the Idaho case, sales price for pototoes grown on a specified field was set upon delivery in the fall with at least 25 percent of the money to be paid in the next calendar year.
